clue.text: He with a pole or perch was such a ruler

definitions.text: He with a pole or perch was such a ruler

parts.words: He with a pole or perch was such a ruler
parts.note: a pole or perch is a quarter of a surveyor's chain, so the clue describes a man who rules a quarter, a title from the Roman world

explanation.surface: A riddle about some lord whose emblem was a rod or a perch.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole and perch look like a bird's roost or a staff of office, but both are old measures equal to a rod, and four rods make a chain. 'He with a quarter' is the ruler of a fourth part of a province.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman empire a governor of one of four divisions of a province held this title; Herod Antipas is the famous example.

clue.text: Resolution for London's financial centre to undergo a clear-up

indicators.note: to undergo is taken as to go under, so the City sits beneath the other pieces in the down entry
up in a down clue says the pair of pieces is read from bottom to top

parts.note: net means clear, as in net profit after deductions
the City is the financial district of London

explanation.surface: Determination for the Square Mile to face a cleanup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns A NET into TENA; 'to undergo' puts CITY beneath it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolution here is firmness of purpose, the quality of holding on doggedly.

clue.text: Keen to charm those Russian leaders first

indicators.note: first places those opening letters ahead of the word for charm
leaders means the opening letters of the two words before it

parts.note: to enchant is to charm

explanation.surface: Eager to win over the bosses in Moscow before anyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A keen blade or a keen remark is sharp and cutting, which is what the word means.

clue.text: Very musical, though a little lacking in attack

indicators.note: a little lacking says a small bit, the final letter, is missing from the word for attack

parts.note: to assail is to attack

explanation.surface: Extremely melodious, though the assault falls a bit short.
explanation.walkthrough: ASSAIL loses its last letter L. 'musical' marks the definition as a term from musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: In scores, the Italian word for very, as in allegro assai.

clue.text: Instrument requiring manipulation of bow in small room?

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the small room

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

indicators.note: manipulation means working the letters by hand into a new order

explanation.surface: A player handling a bow in a cramped practice room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manipulation of' rearranges the letters of 'bow'; the question mark flags that the instrument is not one played with a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell hung round a cow's neck, also played as a percussion instrument in Latin music.

clue.text: Noted work in issue a volunteer force printed

parts.note: issue means offspring, here a son
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about offspring and a volunteer army appearing in print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' is a pun: a work set down in musical notes. 'in' and 'printed' only join the pieces into a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition for one or two instruments in several movements is a classic written-out piece of music.

clue.text: Complaints referee writing about American friend in the sultanate

indicators.note: in places that combination inside the name of the sultanate

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate in Arabia

indicators.note: about means the writing goes round the friend

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
bud is American slang for buddy, a friend

explanation.surface: An arbiter writing about a Yankee pal living in an Arabian state.
explanation.walkthrough: The writing goes 'about' the friend, and that pair goes 'in' the sultanate's name, which splits open after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An official appointed to investigate grievances against public bodies is an adjudicator of complaints.

clue.text: Scene of conflict a long time over

indicators.note: over in a down clue says the phrase is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a long time is an era, written with its article

explanation.surface: A battlefield where ages have passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a long time' is AN ERA; 'over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a sanded space for gladiators, figuratively any field of contest or struggle.

clue.text: Some talk a little of its basic solubility

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A chemist chatting briefly about how basic substances dissolve.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: chemists class this kind of substance as a base that dissolves in water.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemists call a water-soluble base by this name, so the clue's phrase about basic solubility describes it.

clue.text: Walton, for one — no good in real difficulty

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the rearranged letters
in difficulty suggests the letters of real are in trouble and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone like Walton finds nothing goes right when trouble strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: Izaak Walton wrote The Compleat Angler, the classic book on fishing. 'difficulty' rearranges REAL into ALER, with NG put 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Izaak Walton is the archetypal fisherman, an example of the class.

clue.text: Observed returning without daughter's requirements

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the reversed word wraps round the daughter
returning asks for the word meaning observed to be read from its end back to its start

parts.note: observed means seen
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone noticed that a girl's needs went unmet on her return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside': NEES (SEEN read backwards, from 'returning') goes round D.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural nouns for things that are necessary or wanted, the same sense as wants or necessities.

clue.text: Novel brew — a kind protecting us from the weather

indicators.note: novel means new, so the following letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A new beer, a variety that keeps out the cold and rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book or simply 'new brew', but signals the rearrangement of BREW, A and KIND.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge, fence or line of trees that shelters against gusts is described by its job of shielding people from the elements.

clue.text: Colour of carbonaceous rock around a Dorset ravine

indicators.note: around tells us the rock is placed on both sides of the ravine

parts.note: coal is a rock made mostly of carbon
a chine is a narrow coastal ravine, a word used in Dorset and the Isle of Wight

explanation.surface: A shade found in dark rock lining a gorge on England's south coast.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHINE is a steep cleft running down to the sea on the Dorset and Hampshire coasts; Dorset is a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A crimson dye made from crushed scale insects, used to tint food and cloth.

clue.text: An attraction to many, this sort of delivery

parts.note: a draw is something that attracts crowds
L is fifty in Roman numerals, standing for a large number

explanation.surface: A speaking style that charms a great many listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' looks like post or a cricket ball but means a manner of speaking. L for 'many' relies on the Roman numeral fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow lazy way of speaking with drawn-out vowels is a manner of delivering speech.

clue.text: After breaking up, University student is sad

indicators.note: breaking up says the letters of the first word are broken and reassembled

parts.note: L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: After the term ends, a college student feels low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After breaking up' reads as the end of a term, but 'breaking up' rearranges the word 'After' itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the verge of crying is the outward sign of being unhappy.

clue.text: Fish on the Continent, being self-employed?

indicators.note: on here means set on or within, so the fish goes into the country

parts.note: to a Briton the Continent is mainland Europe, here represented by France
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Catching fish abroad as a self-employed worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish on the Continent' reads as foreign seafood; to a Briton 'the Continent' is mainland Europe, here France, and 'on' puts the fish inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who sells services to many clients rather than holding a salaried post.

clue.text: Such control over TV channels makes one aloof

definitions.meaning: a hand-held device for changing channels from a distance
aloof means distant and standoffish in manner

explanation.surface: A clicker in hand turns a person into a detached figure.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is operation from a distance, as with a television handset; the other describes a cool, distant personality.

clue.text: Pose with 24, perhaps, and play a waiting game

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters are just one possible arrangement and must be reordered

parts.note: the answer to 24 down, which is a word for pay

explanation.surface: Strike a pose alongside an earlier clue and hold off.
explanation.walkthrough: The 24 points to 24 down, REMIT; its letters plus POSE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To delay or be evasive in order to gain time is to stall.

clue.text: Where sailors off Hampshire may be abusive

definitions.text: Where sailors off Hampshire may be
definitions.meaning: in the strait between Hampshire's coast and the Isle of Wight, read as two words

explanation.surface: Seamen off the south coast turn foul-mouthed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the strait between mainland Hampshire, a county in southern England, and the Isle of Wight, so sailors there are 'in Solent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words the answer places sailors in that strait; as one word it means rudely disrespectful.

clue.text: Lay emphasis on mechanical force

definitions.meaning: in engineering, force per unit area acting within a material

explanation.surface: An engineer underlining the importance of physical loads.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to emphasise; as a noun in physics it is the internal force a load puts on a body.

clue.text: Nurse who in Paris invested in a dress ornament

indicators.note: invested in means clothed inside, so the French word goes within the nurse

parts.note: SEN was a State Enrolled Nurse in Britain
qui is French for who

explanation.surface: A nurse in Paris spending on a sparkly frock trim.
explanation.walkthrough: SEN, a State Enrolled Nurse, was a British nursing grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A small shiny disc sewn on clothing as decoration.

clue.text: Slave or servant on duty

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the servant after the word for duty

parts.note: a bond is a binding obligation or duty
a man is a manservant

explanation.surface: Whether bonded slave or working servant, both are at their posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is only a link: 'servant on duty' is the wordplay, with the servant coming on after the duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A man bound to serve without wages, a serf or bondsman, is an unfree labourer.

clue.text: Lodger finds key in flower-bed

indicators.note: in places the key inside the flower-bed

parts.note: a border is a strip of garden planted with flowers
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: A tenant finds the house key in the garden bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like a door key but is the musical key A.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who pays for room and meals in someone else's home.

clue.text: Club that's shortly to support a TV programme

indicators.note: to support in a down clue puts the second piece underneath the first

parts.note: M*A*S*H was a long-running TV comedy about an army hospital
ie is the short form of that is

explanation.surface: A golf club sponsoring a television show.
explanation.definitionFit: An old golf iron with a lofted face, roughly a modern five iron.

clue.text: Sounds like an examination of the ear

indicators.note: Sounds like says the word for a spoken test is said aloud to give a different spelling

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A spoken test that sounds as if a doctor were inspecting your hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like an examination of the ear' reads as a hearing test; in fact 'of the ear' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to hearing, from the Latin for ear.

clue.text: Pay race official for turning up

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from end to start

parts.note: a timer clocks the runners in a race

explanation.surface: Paying the man with the stopwatch for showing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' looks like arriving but reverses TIMER.
explanation.definitionFit: To send money in payment is to remit it.

clue.text: Low Sunday bell-ringer at Notre Dame?

definitions.meaning: the first Sunday after Easter, named in the Church from the opening words of its Latin introit
the hunchback who rings the bells in Victor Hugo's novel

explanation.surface: A quiet church day for the famous Paris bell-ringer.
explanation.definitionFit: Low Sunday is also called by this Latin name from its introit, and Hugo named his foundling hunchback after the day he was found.

clue.text: As a precaution, detailed these Peruvian people

indicators.note: detailed means having its tail, the last letter, cut off

parts.note: in case means as a precaution

explanation.surface: Being careful, someone itemised these people of Peru.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'thorough' but means de-tailed: IN CASE loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andean civilisation centred on Cuzco whose empire ruled Peru before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: People producing a low-frequency noise — a new variety

parts.note: a hum is a low droning sound
kind means sort or variety

explanation.surface: Folk making a droning sound in a fresh fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective term for the human race, everybody taken together.

clue.text: This man's copyright not recorded

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for copyright, as in the circled C
a live broadcast is not recorded

explanation.surface: A man whose rights were never put on tape.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's given name, so it can stand for some particular man.

clue.text: Right of admission to an intermediate course

definitions.meaning: the right or privilege of entering somewhere
in older dining, a dish served between the fish and the main roast

explanation.surface: A ticket that admits you to the middle part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for entry means both access to a place and a dish served between courses.

clue.text: What one anticipates in a school brochure? Not us

indicators.note: Not tells us to take the following word out of the brochure

parts.note: a prospectus is a booklet describing a school to prospective pupils

explanation.surface: A school booklet's promise of what to expect, though not about us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not us' removes US from the end of PROSPECTUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An expectation of some future event, as in the likelihood of success.
